core/export_gate.py - the export-time secondary quantity interception.

The synthesis gate (``recipe_synth.verify_recipe``) already proves a recipe
reproduces the AI-read totals before it enters the cache. This module is the
SECOND interception, run at export time over the current batch only
(``self.results``), so a later edit, a value-clean transform, or a stale cache
can never ship a silently wrong quantity.

What it checks (all quantity-focused, customer-agnostic):

  * HARD (blocks export unless the operator explicitly releases):
      - colour/size breakdown mismatches vs the PDF's printed subtotals
        (``validate_breakdown`` - gated by the AI-set recipe flags);
      - a parsed total of 0 (nothing usable to export);
      - any negative quantity (clearly wrong).
  * SOFT (advisory, never blocks):
      - the structural/price-coverage warnings from ``validate.reconcile``.

A single batch may contain several POs; the gate aggregates every hard problem
and presents them in one modal so the operator decides once.
Result of the export-time quantity check for ONE purchase order.

    ``source`` is the original file name, shown in the dialog for context.

Pre-scan an entire batch before export, partitioning it into records that
    pass the quantity interception and records that contain hard blocks.

    ``results`` is the same list-of-dicts shape as ``MainWindow.results``
    (keys: po, recipe, path, ...). Records with no parseable ``po``/``recipe`` are
    treated as passable (the downstream writer will surface any real error), so
    the gate never silently drops an unparsed file. Returns ``(ok, blocked)``
    where ``ok`` is the list of source records to export and ``blocked`` is the
    list of :class:`ExportGateReport` that carry hard blocks.
